note.text: Support begins by asking what a person needs and respecting their choices. Age, illness or disability does not remove a person's dignity or make every person need the same assistance. Discuss practical help, permission, clear communication and when to seek a responsible adult. This lesson teaches respectful English rather than medical care. Learners should not lift people, administer treatment or take over an adult's responsibilities as a classroom exercise.

sections.heading: Understand the ideas
sections.text: Support begins by asking what a person needs and respecting their choices. Age, illness or disability does not remove a person's dignity or make every person need the same assistance. Discuss practical help, permission, clear communication and when to seek a responsible adult. This lesson teaches respectful English rather than medical care. Learners should not lift people, administer treatment or take over an adult's responsibilities as a classroom exercise.

sections.heading: Apply the ideas locally
sections.text: Original dialogue: Ayuk asks an older neighbour, Would you like help carrying that light bag? The neighbour accepts and names where to put it. Bih asks a classmate which route is accessible rather than assuming what the classmate can do. If a younger sibling becomes unwell, a learner tells a responsible adult rather than guessing a treatment.

sections.heading: Reason and check
sections.text: Choose wording that offers rather than imposes help. Listen to the answer and avoid speaking about a present person as though absent. In a discussion, distinguish an observation from an assumption and keep personal health details private.
